items.text: A second overnight strike on the [[p:Crimean Bridge]] {{note: Road and rail bridge over the Kerch Strait that Russia opened in 2018, four years after annexing Crimea.}} brought down one arch and a stretch of roadway; Russia's Transport Ministry suspended traffic and reported no casualties. Kyiv Independent says a Ukrainian Flamingo missile was used. The same night Russian ballistic missiles hit two Kyiv bridges over the Dnipro, Mayor [[p:Vitali Klitschko]] says, disrupting water, heating and the metro; Ukrainian officials report two dead.
items.notes: Missile type per Kyiv Independent; not confirmed by Kyiv officially.

items.text: [[p:Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] says Ukraine held new online peace talks with US envoys [[p:Steve Witkoff]] and [[p:Jared Kushner]] and European officials, and that Ukrainian intelligence shows North Korea supplying Russia with new ballistic missiles. Axios reports the envoys will meet Ukrainian and European officials in Berlin on 19 Nov on security guarantees; the Ramstein-format contact group meets at NATO on 17 Nov.

The bulk carrier Betul 8, carrying Romanian wheat to Egypt, capsized and sank in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone after its crew reported two sea-drone hits; all 12 crew were rescued. Security firm Diaplous counts 17 vessels attacked off Bulgaria and Romania since July. Officials in both countries point at Russia, but Sofia says there is no proof; Moscow has denied earlier attacks.

[[p:Donald Trump]] arrived in Manila for the ASEAN–US special summit and the first in-person [[p:Quad|Quadrilateral Security Dialogue]] leaders' meeting since 2024, with [[p:Narendra Modi]], [[p:Sanae Takaichi]] and [[p:Anthony Albanese]]. The White House itinerary then takes him to Shenzhen for [[p:APEC|Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation]], with a first Trump–[[p:Xi Jinping]]–[[p:Vladimir Putin]] meeting planned for 19 Nov; Trump says he might also meet [[p:Kim Jong Un]].

Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands unveiled in Vienna a plan for a return hub in Rwanda for rejected asylum seekers, the first outside the EU, starting with a pilot of about 100 people in 2027 under the tightened EU return rules. UNHCR said it must respect human rights law; [[p:Human Rights Watch]] and NGOs criticised it and Spain rejected it.

The [[p:Sudanese Armed Forces]] are pushing into West Kordofan towards En Nahud, a gold hub that helps fund the [[p:Rapid Support Forces]]; the army says it took Al-Khuwai on 13 Nov and an RSF commander in North Darfur announced his defection. The Emergency Lawyers group blames an army airstrike in Abu Zabad for at least 13 deaths, which AP could not verify.
items.notes: Battlefield claims by the army; casualty claim by a rights group.

items.text: Parliament speaker and chief negotiator [[p:Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf]] says Iran sent seven conditions through Qatar, including lifting the blockade and sanctions, releasing frozen funds and formally ending the war on all fronts, and that 'the ball is in the American court'. Qatar says both sides responded positively to its mediation, but by 17 Nov no formal US reply had been reported; [[p:Marco Rubio]] calls the demands unacceptable.
items.notes: Al Jazeera piece is analysis. An unconfirmed 3 Nov report (Pakistan Today via Al-Araby Al-Jadeed) said the US approved the Qatari draft; later reporting treats the US position as pending.

items.text: Deputy FM [[p:Kazem Gharibabadi]] said Iran 'will not wait for the US to attack first' and that the [[p:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps|IRGC]] is producing missiles with new ranges. In Washington, Rubio said economic pressure makes large-scale strikes unnecessary and Vice President [[p:JD Vance]] said the conflict will not become a 'forever war'.
items.notes: Venue/date of Gharibabadi remark not given.

items.text: The IRGC says it attacked a US radar at Isa Air Base in Bahrain, state broadcaster IRIB reports; Bahrain says its air defences thwarted the drone attack after explosions were heard over Manama. It is the third IRGC strike on Bahrain claimed since 13 Nov.
items.notes: No US comment yet. 13 Nov: CENTCOM said it downed two drones with no damage.

items.text: UKMTO reported an outbound tanker struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, causing an engine-room fire; all crew were accounted for and no one claimed the attack.
ADNOC Logistics & Services said one of its vessels was damaged in an attack in the Gulf; UKMTO separately reported a tanker hit by a projectile off Lima, Oman, with crew safe. No attacker was named.

At the [[p:Economic Cooperation Organization]] ministerial in Islamabad, [[p:Abbas Araghchi]] called for a regional security framework and energy mechanism and blamed the US and Israel for disruption at Hormuz; Pakistan's [[p:Ishaq Dar]] pledged continued de-escalation efforts.
Rights group Hengaw reports three murder convicts, including two women, hanged in Shiraz, plus other mid-November executions in several cities; Iranian authorities have not announced them.

[[p:Gulf Cooperation Council|GCC]] defence ministers approved a forward headquarters for the bloc's Unified Military Command in Kuwait, with forces assigned; size and site were not disclosed. Secretary-General Jasem Albudaiwi condemned Iranian attacks on member states.

Bahrain's High Criminal Court sentenced 64 defendants, mostly Shia clerics of the dissolved Ulema Council, to life and five to 15 years for forming an IRGC-linked 'Wilayat al-Faqih' organisation, per the state news agency.
items.outlet: Middle East Monitor (citing Bahrain News Agency)
items.notes: Some tried in absentia. No rights-group reaction found yet.

items.text: Iraq reopened the Al-Sheeb crossing with Iran and closed Mandali from 13 Nov for 'technical requirements'; Iran put its Khosravi crossing on 24-hour operation. FM [[p:Fuad Hussein]] says closing all crossings as the US Treasury asks would hurt Iraq. No further closures were found through 17 Nov.

Security sources tell Alhurra that PM Ali al-Zaidi postponed a three-brigade operation on Jurf al-Sakhar, the stronghold of [[p:Kata'ib Hezbollah]], after the plan leaked to [[p:Popular Mobilization Forces|PMF]] leaders. An investigative committee then entered the area over oil smuggling, and Babil's governor resigned.
items.notes: Translated from Arabic. Postponement rests on unnamed sources; Alhurra is US government-funded.

items.text: Government spokesman Haider al-Aboudi says the army will enter Jurf al-Sakhar after a committee found pipeline tapping, two refineries and fuel stores; The National reports a withdrawal deadline of 8pm on 20 Nov. A ruling-alliance meeting broke up when [[p:Hadi al-Amiri]] walked out; Kata'ib Hezbollah denies smuggling.
items.notes: Deadline reported inconsistently (Shafaq: 20 Nov; 964: no date).

items.text: Government-aligned Southern forces withdrew from Dhubab and the Bab al-Mandeb area to defend Aden, ending a six-week Red Sea coast counteroffensive. Reuters puts [[p:Houthis|Houthi]] forces about 80 km from Aden in Lahj while Taiz stays encircled; the government calls it a 'tactical manoeuvre'.
items.notes: Distances conflict: Reuters 80 km / al-Suqyah 150 km west of Aden; Long War Journal ~40 miles. Displacement 300,000 (Reuters) vs 340,000+ (OCHA).

items.text: The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted two Houthi drones over Mecca and Riyadh regions; Houthi spokesman [[p:Yahya Saree]] claims 88 Saudi airstrikes that day.
The [[p:United Nations Security Council|UN Security Council]] unanimously renewed Yemen sanctions for a year, extending the Panel of Experts and condemning Houthi escalation.
